x: Four teams started in this race but unfortunately Bob McMullen and Hugh McGreechan were unable to get there which made a considerable difference to our chances in the scratch race.

…oing to come out winners until the very end, eventually 3 points separated the first 3 teams with us taking 3rd place.. Bob McMullen once again led the lads home in 5th position with George Checkley 8th, Hugh McGreechan 15th and E.…

Bob McMullen, 10th, led the "A" team home followed by Syd James, 11th, George Checkley.14th, and Eric Hall 20th, the next three places being filled by Phillips, Brian Shepherd (second claim) and Hugh McGreechan

A total of 51 completed the course, and we filled the first three places with Bob McMullen 97.53,S.James 98.18 and Hugh McGreechan 99.02. The next three places were filled by Surrey and then three more for us - Guilmant, Eglington and Demmon.

We had great hopes however, of a placing with Stan Vickers, and Eric Hall, Kent and Surrey Champions, Syd James 2nd in the Surrey, George Checkley 5th in the Middlesex and Bob McMullen back from Canada and showing something like his old form, together with George Beecham, young Terry Clark and Ted Smith.
Bob McMullen with a generous 5 minutes, took first prize, with Ron West 2nd and Ted Smith 3rd.

At 5 miles, Eric Hall, George Checkley, Davis of Woodford Green and Bob McMullen led the field with Beecham moving up. Harry was still hanging back, but catching sight of Fred Rolfe and Doub he put on pressure and soon passed them.

In the absence of the holder Harold King,Bob McMullen won the club"10" walk in 82:24. Nearly 100 members,friends and visitors were present at the Club dinner amongst whom were W.J.Pepper, J.Binks, E.H.Neville, W.F.May, E.H.Collden, W.C.Jewell,and W.J.Palmer.

How nice to see Bob McMullen (now on the 80 mark) and Harry Churcher (Seven times A.A.A. Champion and an Olympic walker) who was prevailed upon to present the awards, and Joe Coleman, Ben Knifton, Tom Scrimshaw, Percy Wright, Harold King - and no doubt old Uncle Tom Cobley was there as well!
That well known veteran walker DAVE McMULLEN tells us that his father BOB McMULLEN, now over 80, is still active and well and enjoys a game of golf at Mitcham.
It was then a unique double for a 21 year old, thanks to training with Bob McMullen & Co. My son John surpassed me as an athlete and was in many of the Club's winning teams.
